summary: This short wiki note covers the academic background of Lawrence Landweber. It states that he earned a bachelor's degree from Brooklyn College in 1963 and a Ph.D. from Purdue University in 1967. It also gives the title of his doctoral thesis, which concerns a design algorithm for sequential machines and definability in monadic second-order arithmetic.
one_line: Lawrence Landweber's education: Brooklyn College bachelor's (1963) and Purdue Ph.D. (1967) with a thesis on sequential machines.
key_facts: Lawrence Landweber received his bachelor's degree in 1963 at Brooklyn College.
Lawrence Landweber received his Ph.D. at Purdue University in 1967.
The doctoral thesis of Lawrence Landweber is titled "A design algorithm for sequential machines and definability in monadic second-order arithmetic."
The thesis topic covers a design algorithm for sequential machines.
The thesis topic also covers definability in monadic second-order arithmetic.
Brooklyn College is where Lawrence Landweber completed his bachelor's degree.
Purdue University is where Lawrence Landweber completed his doctoral studies.
The note gives no information about Lawrence Landweber's career or later work.
